Organising the data

Source: vignettes/organising-data.Rmd
organising-data.Rmd

sheepdog never asks for a project file or a database: it reads folders and tables, and takes the site, the night and the hour from where the files are and from their names. This article describes the layout it expects, how the paths written by BirdNET are matched to the audio, and how to build the list of all recordings that some designs need.

Three folders

A project has three kinds of files, and each lives best in its own folder:

audio/                            recordings, never modified
  ARA/
    ARA01_20211001_190000.wav
    ...
  BAI/
    card1/BAI01_20211001_190000.wav
    card2/...
birdnet/                          BirdNET output, one run per site
  ARA/BirdNET_SelectionTable.txt  a combined table per site, or
  BAI/BAI01_20211001_190000.BirdNET.selection.table.txt
                                  one table per audio file
validation/                       what sheepdog writes
  clip_manifest.csv
  clips/<species>/...             clips to review
  ...
  • Audio. One folder per site, with any subfolders below it (memory cards, dates). The site is the first folder below the root. Recordings are only read, never moved or renamed.
  • BirdNET output. Run BirdNET once per site, so that the selection tables of each site end up in their own folder: read_selection_tables() takes the site from the name of the folder that holds the tables (the prefix output_ is dropped). Both the combined table and the per-audio tables of the BirdNET GUI are read.
  • Several sites in one folder. When the recordings or the tables of several sites sit in the same folder, give site_pattern, a regular expression with the site in parentheses, to list_recordings(), read_selection_tables() and run_app(): "^[^_]+_([^_]+)_" reads Campus01 from Campinas_Campus01_20261003_074339.flac. The site then comes from the file name instead of the folder.
  • sheepdog outputs. Clips, manifests, verdicts and calibration outputs go to a separate folder, so that a rerun never touches the audio or the BirdNET output.

The site names must be the same in the three places: the folder names of the audio and of the BirdNET output, and later the site column of every table.

File names

The night and the hour come from the name of each recording, which must carry the date and time as YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS, as most recorders (AudioMoth, Song Meter and others) write them: ARA01_20211001_190000.wav was recorded on 1 October 2021 at 19:00. In the calibration, recordings that start before dawn_hour belong to the night before. Do not rename the recordings after running BirdNET: the selection tables keep the original path.

Paths written by BirdNET

Every selection table has a Begin Path column with the full path of the audio file as BirdNET saw it, for example N:\pam\audio\ARA\ARA01_...wav on the Windows computer that ran the analysis. sheepdog uses that path to cut the clips and to match the predictions to the list of recordings. When the audio is reached by another path (another computer, a drive mounted elsewhere), pass the old and the new prefix to remap_from and remap_to:

man <- select_clips(pred, "random_detections", threshold = 0.5,
                    remap_from = "N:/pam/audio/",
                    remap_to = "/Volumes/NAS/pam/audio/")

Backslashes are turned into forward slashes before the prefix is replaced.

The list of all recordings

"random_recordings" in select_clips(), the occasions of export_occupancy_data() and the sampling tab of run_app() need the list of every recording made, including the ones in which BirdNET predicted nothing. Without it, those functions list the audio files of the folders that appear in Begin Path, which leaves out any folder without a single prediction. list_recordings() builds the list from the audio folders instead. Here on a small simulated tree:

library(sheepdog)

audio <- file.path(tempdir(), "audio")
for (s in c("ARA", "BAI/card1")) dir.create(file.path(audio, s),
                                            recursive = TRUE)
invisible(file.create(
  file.path(audio, "ARA", c("ARA01_20211001_190000.wav",
                            "ARA01_20211001_200000.wav")),
  file.path(audio, "BAI", "card1", "BAI01_20211001_190000.wav")))

rec <- list_recordings(audio)
#> 3 recordings listed at 2 site(s).
rec
#> # A tibble: 3 × 2
#>   site  source_audio                                             
#>   <chr> <chr>                                                    
#> 1 ARA   /tmp/RtmptZCNct/audio/ARA/ARA01_20211001_190000.wav      
#> 2 ARA   /tmp/RtmptZCNct/audio/ARA/ARA01_20211001_200000.wav      
#> 3 BAI   /tmp/RtmptZCNct/audio/BAI/card1/BAI01_20211001_190000.wav

The paths must match Begin Path. When the list is built on a computer other than the one that ran BirdNET, rewrite the prefix with remap_from and remap_to, and give the predictions to check the match; the message says how many of their audio files are in the list:

pred <- read_selection_tables("birdnet")
rec <- list_recordings("/Volumes/NAS/pam/audio",
                       remap_from = "/Volumes/NAS/pam/audio/",
                       remap_to = "N:/pam/audio/",
                       predictions = pred,
                       file = "validation/recordings.csv")

The alternative is to keep the local paths in the list and pass the same remap_from and remap_to to select_clips(), which then rewrites Begin Path to the local prefix. Either way, the CSV written with file can be given as recordings to select_clips(), export_occupancy_data() and run_app().

Where each function looks

step function reads writes
read predictions read_selection_tables() birdnet/<site>/ a table in R
list recordings list_recordings() audio/<site>/ recordings.csv
choose clips select_clips() predictions, recordings a manifest in R
cut clips cut_clips(), extract_validation_clips() the audio, through Begin Path clips/<species>/, clip_manifest.csv
review file manager (Positive/Negative subfolders) or run_app() clips, manifest folders, or a verdicts CSV
join verdicts post_validation() review folder or verdicts.csv, manifest validation_by_clip.csv and summaries
calibrate calibrate() validation_by_clip.csv, selection tables calibration outputs, detection histories

See vignette("sheepdog") for the whole pipeline on the example data and vignette("frognet-workflow") for a project with a network drive mapped as N:.
